text: {"foundGenuineWeakness":true,"weaknessDescription":"A specific and real limitation, which is not the same as a refutation. (1) The pooled evidence is entirely observational: five cohort and five case-control studies, no randomised allocation anywhere in the set. Vaccination status is not assigned, so it correlates with whatever else distinguishes families who vaccinate on schedule, including healthcare contact, socioeconomic position and baseline health. A healthy-vaccinee effect of that kind biases toward the null, and nothing in this record measures or adjusts it away. (2) Exposure definitions are heterogeneous across the constituent studies, covering MMR specifically, thimerosal specifically, and cumulative vaccine exposure. Pooling a narrow exposure into a broad one dilutes a subgroup effect toward null by construction, so a genuine association confined to one exposure or one susceptible subgroup could survive as a null pooled estimate. (3) Pre-specification of the pooling protocol is not evidenced, so inclusion and exposure-definition choices were available to be made after the constituent results were known. None of this shows the pooled conclusion is wrong, and the registry cohorts are large; it shows the design cannot by itself exclude a small or subgroup-confined effect, which is exactly the residue an adversarial pass should surface rather than wave away."}
